Easy

1EasyCompute

A small economy has consumption C=250C = 250C=250, investment I=100I = 100I=100, government spending G=90G = 90G=90, and net exports NX=−40NX = -40NX=−40.

Find GDP and the consumption share.

  • The Circle Money Travels: GDP
Show solution

  1. GDP is the sum of spending: 250+100+90−40=400250 + 100 + 90 - 40 = 400250+100+90−40=400.

  2. The consumption share is 250/400=0.625250 / 400 = 0.625250/400=0.625, that is 62.5%62.5\%62.5%. Even with negative net exports, consumption still fills most of the circle.

Answer

GDP=400GDP = 400GDP=400

Medium

2Medium

A demand shock sets the output gap to −5%-5\%−5%.

(1) In the Keynesian world, what is the gap after 101010 periods?

(2) In the New Keynesian world, what are the gap and the price level (starting at 100100100) after 333 periods?

  • One Shock, Three Schools
Show solution

  1. (1) Keynes treats prices as frozen (λ=0\lambda = 0λ=0). The gap is gt=−5⋅(1−0)t=−5g_t = -5 \cdot (1 - 0)^t = -5gt​=−5⋅(1−0)t=−5 — after 101010 periods it is exactly where it started.

  2. (2) In the New Keynesian world the gap shrinks to 0.60.60.6 of itself each period: g3=−5⋅0.63=−5⋅0.216=−1.08%g_3 = -5 \cdot 0.6^3 = -5 \cdot 0.216 = -1.08\%g3​=−5⋅0.63=−5⋅0.216=−1.08%.

    Meanwhile prices fall by 5⋅(1−0.216)=3.925 \cdot (1 - 0.216) = 3.925⋅(1−0.216)=3.92, leaving the price level at 100−3.92=96.08100 - 3.92 = 96.08100−3.92=96.08.

    The remaining gap, 1.081.081.08, plus what prices absorbed, 3.923.923.92, adds back up to exactly the shock, 555.
